# The forwarding-filter policy combines menu hiding with a successful backend no-op

The policy requests a locked false mail.filters.forward.enabled preference. CSS hides the filter editor forwarding item, while ForwardMessage separately returns NS_OK before sending when that preference is false. Actual filter callers share this service, so the guard also covers their existing actions without reporting an error that would stop later permitted actions. The new IMAP test directly checks no SMTP post and a following MarkRead action; the browser test checks computed menu/separator display. Existing action serialization does not add a policy save rejection or remove stored definitions. These are static contracts and test oracles, not fresh sending, policy-engine, keyboard or accessibility results.

Scope: Enterprise policy and message-filter forwarding enforcement.
